title: Token alias collision — staggered rollout debug notes
content:
Summary:

Short version: during a staggered rollout of v1.1 tokenizers paired with a quantized weight swap for model X, the canary population exhibited a subtle token aliasing issue that changed punctuation token IDs for a small subset (~0.4%) of requests. This produced downstream decoding artifacts (extra leading whitespace + occasional duplicated punctuation) and a measurable regression in decode quality metrics for the canary cohort. No crash/failure of serving infra; impact was user-facing quality degradation only.

Why this doc exists:
- Capture detection timeline and quick mitigations we used on-call.
- Draft a runbook amendment for tokenizer/model compatibility checks.
- Propose long-term fixes (validation tooling + automatic gating).

Detection and impact:
- 2024-11-09 20:48 UTC — Synthetic QA monitor alerted: p95 decode-bleu delta > 0.15 on canary-hostgroup-2.
- 2024-11-09 20:53 UTC — SRE oncall (Jordan) confirmed increased "weird punctuation" customer reports in error-tracker.
- 2024-11-09 21:00 UTC — Telemetry showed 0.36% of requests in canary cohort had token ID sequences that did not match expected mapping; symptoms: extra spaces before commas/periods and occasional "!!" duplication.
- 2024-11-09 21:15 UTC — Scoped: only canary hostgroup-2 (10 nodes) running tokenizer v1.1 + model quantized weights q4_128. All other hostgroups on tokenizer v1.0 + same weights were fine.
- Business impact: minor quality regression for small fraction of requests in canary; no downtime. CS received 7 reports in the hour (internal triage).

Initial hypothesis:
- Tokenizer v1.1 introduced a remapping of a few punctuation subtokens (split/merge changes). Quantized weight binary expects token ID ordering consistent with model vocab mapping used during compile/kv-cache generation. During batched decode path, a mismatch between tokenizer-vocab and runtime token-index mapping leads to occasional index-offset in the decoder for small batches when prefix-caching hits combine with continuous batching boundary conditions.

Quick evidence gathered:
- grep of tokenizer binary builds showed new merges: "'.' + '…'" merge pattern changed indexes for subtokens 402..407.
- Runtime logs (snippet):
  [2024-11-09T20:52:31Z] decode: request_id=rq_98a1 token_ids=[502, 12, 403, 1101, 2]
  [2024-11-09T20:52:31Z] tokenizer (v1.0) -> detokenized: 'We shipped.'
  [2024-11-09T20:52:31Z] tokenizer (v1.1) -> detokenized: 'We shipped .'
- Repro script: using a small corpus of strings with punctuation we could consistently reproduce alias output when combining prefix cache hit + microbatch size 4 and kernel path A (fast-attn).

Root cause (current working understanding):
1) Tokenizer v1.1 changed subtoken ID assignments for a small punctuations set.
2) During packaging, the quantized weight artifact included a token-index remap table generated against tokenizer v1.0. We failed to regenerate the remap/table after tokenizer change.
3) Runtime's KV cache and continuous-batching logic assumed remap invariants; for certain microbatch ordering/prefix-hit cases the remap was applied incorrectly leading to off-by-one token indices fed to the decoder.
4) Manifest-level validation (weight checksum + tokenizer checksum) existed but compared file-level SHA only for weights not internal token-index mapping; this gap allowed deployment to proceed.

Why this slipped past tests:
- Unit tests validate end-to-end decode using canonical prompts but not under combined conditions: prefix cache hit + small microbatches + kernel A.
- Local preflight used deterministic batching (single request) and missed concurrency ordering case.

Immediate mitigations (what we did on-call):
- 21:30 UTC — Disable tokenizer v1.1 rollout (stopped staged rollout at 3/10 hosts).
- 21:45 UTC — Rollback canary-hostgroup-2 to tokenizer v1.0 (config flag: tokenizer.active_version=head:1.0) via orchestration quick-rollback. Completed by 21:58 UTC.
- 22:10 UTC — Disabled automatic weight remap optimization for the next model push (runtime flag: remap_optimize=false) to avoid malformed remap behavior.
- 22:30 UTC — Enabled additional logging guarded by sample-rate 1% focusing on token-id->string mapping for requests hitting prefix cache.
- Notified product and CS; routed customer reports to CS triage.

What prevented escalation:
- Canary isolation and quick rollback were effective. No global rollout occurred. The anomaly surface area was small.

Post-incident analysis steps (done/ongoing):
- 11/10 — Reproduced issue locally with reproducible script (mateo). Confirmed remap mismatch is root cause.
- 11/11 — Added unit test covering case: prefix-cache + microbatch size <=4 + kernel A, comparing detokenized strings across tokenizer versions and remap table generation.
- 11/11 — Created regression test harness that runs tokenizer-version matrix × weight-artifact remap table check during CI.
- 11/12 — Drafted manifest-level validation (pull request #1892) to include token-index mapping checksum into model artifact manifest.

Short-term action items (owners):
- INF-3421 (Jordan): Add tokenizer-version / token-index checksum to manifest and fail deployment if mismatch. (ETA 2024-11-14)
- RUNTIME-1892 (Mateo): CI job to run reproduction harness across batching/kernels. (ETA 2024-11-13)
- SRE-ops (Aisha): Update runbook "rollout-preflight" to include paired tokenizer/weight checksum check and to run microbatch stress tests on canary before flipping >30% of hosts. (ETA 2024-11-16)
- PRODUCT (Priya): Communicate to customers the rollback and that no persistent data was effected. (ETA 2024-11-12)
- ENG (Samira): Add sampling logs for token-id mapping to observability dashboards (p95/p99 mismatch rate). (ETA 2024-11-18)

Longer-term proposals (discussion items):
- Enforce artifact-level bonding: tokenizer build id must be embedded in weight artifact and validated at deploy time.
- Expand preflight to run a small randomized concurrency test matrix (vary microbatch size 1..8, include prefix cache hits and kernel selection toggles). Could be done with a tiny internal load-test harness running in staging.
- Consider moving token-index remap generation into the model compile step (so it's deterministic and versioned with the model) rather than a runtime on-the-fly heuristic.
- Ship a small "compatibility report" page in Redwood Console showing tokenizer vs model artifacts compatibility and a gating flag.

Draft runbook additions (proposal for short checklist):
1) Before tokenizer or vocab change: regenerate remap table and run compatibility job against latest weight artifact.
2) Create a short randomized microbatch test suite (seeded) and run on canary hosts with intended deployment config.
3) Verify manifest includes both tokenizer checksum and remap checksum; block deploy if mismatch.
4) If canary anomalies observed: pause rollout -> snapshot telemetry -> rollback tokenizer version -> disable remap_optimize -> escalate to eng-safety.

Open questions and unresolved items:
- Edge case: could other kernel selection paths (kernel B) hide the bug? We saw it more with kernel A; need to test kernel B/C explicitly.
- Should remap be embedded into weight artifact or kept external? Tradeoffs: size vs portability.
- How to automate detection: what metric thresholds are reliable (currently we used p95 decode-bleu delta and token-id mismatch rate >0.1%).

Appendix: useful commands / snippets
- Repro folder: infra/tests/token-remap-repro/
- quick grep for suspect tokens in logs:
  zgrep -h "token_ids\=\[" /var/log/redwood/runtime/*.log | grep "403, 1101" -n | head
- quick rollback command (internal):
  rcli rollout cancel --target canary-hostgroup-2 --component tokenizer && rcli deploy set-config --group canary-hostgroup-2 tokenizer.active_version=1.0
- CI job link: https://ci.redwood-internal/pipelines/compatibility/jobs/1892

Notes to reviewers:
- This is a working/debug doc. Please add test cases you think are missing in the repro harness.
- If you have a different hypothesis (e.g., a quantization rounding artifact interacting with index mapping), add notes here and tag the linked PRs/jira.

Recent edits log:
- 2024-11-10 (Mateo): added repro steps and local test results.
- 2024-11-11 (Aisha): added runbook checklist draft.
- 2024-11-12 (Jordan): added immediate mitigations timeline and action items.
